explanation: Fires on the word right after a verb of knowing/perceiving/learning (know, see, show, figure out, determine, check out), usually a wh-word such as 'how', 'what', or 'who' that starts an embedded question clause ('knows[[ how]]', 'see[[ what]]'). The context verb drives it: wh-words with no such verb before them, and other complements, give only weak to moderate activation.

Fires on mid-word subword fragments of rare proper names and alphanumeric strings, such as name pieces ('Pr[[AS]]ad', 'O[[ts]]uka', 'Nass'), digits or dots inside version numbers, IPs, ports, hex codes and error codes, plus 'wide' in 'wide receiver'. The common thread seems to be completing a memorized token sequence, but the examples are heterogeneous.

Mixed bag. It fires on 'almost' (strongly and repeatedly), 'template' at the start of C++ declarations, ES/ECMAScript version tokens, and assorted word fragments and function words in technical or scientific prose ('minim[[ally]]', 'Induction[[ of]]', 'Emp[[ress]]'). There is no single shared rule.

Fires on a unit-of-measurement token right after a number, especially mass, concentration and dose units in biomedical text (μ[[g]], micro[[grams]], nm[[ol]], mg, ng, mL, cd, W). Other units after numbers (mm, Gy, km, V, ×) and non-unit tokens give weaker activation.

No coherent pattern. Top examples include a space before a number, word-piece fragments ('hi'atus, 'Mim'ics), 'high' in 'high school' or 'high-frequency', capital 'T' in cell names, and assorted function words across scientific, multilingual and general text.

Fires mainly on tokens inside boilerplate software license and copyright headers ('Software distributed under the License[[ is]]', 'THE SOFTWARE[[ IS]] PROVIDED', the hyphen in 'Copyright 2007[[-]]2017', 'Permission[[ is]] hereby'). It also fires somewhat on predictable continuations of other formulaic phrases; that secondary activity is scattered.

Fires on the final digit of a birth year, or on the en-dash or space right after a birth date, in Wikipedia-style biography openings ('(born October 8, 197[[5]]', '(13 May 1906[[ –]]'). Outside that format it shows only scattered weak activity.

Fires on ellipses ('...', '…') and colons that start a new line or segment after a break (Q&A 'Q[[:]]', Python '...' prompts, continuation ellipses). It fires more weakly on 'to' after 'related' and 'entitled' after a reference to a document.

Fires on words that express plurality, grouping or composite structure, especially 'of' in 'list of', 'course of' and 'string of', plus 'several', 'complex', 'team', 'two bit', 'x' in '4x100', 'array' and 'tandem'. Strength varies, and the examples only loosely share this multiplicity theme.

Fires on the predictable continuation of a fixed multi-token name or phrase: the second half of compounds and identifiers ('Open[[Layers]]', 'son-in[[-law]]', 'Astronaut[[ics]]', 'hex[[2]]dec', 'BGR[[2]]HSV'), and words in boilerplate phrases ('distributed[[ in]] the hope', 'in[[ accordance]]', 'weight[[ loss]]', 'Not[[ surprisingly]]').

Fires on forms of 'keep' (keep, keeping, kept) in the sense of maintaining or retaining something, especially keeping quiet, secret, out or open. It also fires on the token right after 'keep' in idioms ('keeping[[ an]] eye', 'keep[[ a]]') and on related verbs ('stay', 'holding them back', 'maintain'), more weakly.
